aboutIntro: Software developer and Fatec Cotia graduate. My interests range from how systems work to the experience of the people who use them.
aboutParagraphs: I started with an interest in making games, first trying Lua for Roblox, then learning Python through the Ignorância Zero channel. I made Pygame games. Discovering Django led me to HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Git and web development tools.

Python remained my tool for scripts, command-line utilities and exercises. At college I discovered CentOS and switched my personal computer to Ubuntu. I explored networking, servers, Docker, cloud and automation with Ansible, Terraform and Vagrant.

Linux became a key interest. I explored Ubuntu, RHEL, CentOS, Alpine, AlmaLinux, Fedora and Arch, alongside shell, permissions, firewalls, web servers and virtual-machine labs. I am studying for LPIC-1 and deepening my networking knowledge.

Wanting to understand how things work led me to Rust, my favorite language. I created Textforge, a small language for batch text processing through descriptive pipelines, published on crates.io. Python and Node.js bindings are in development.
During my Fatec internship I worked on an asset and inventory management system with TypeScript, NestJS and React, accompanied by a Kotlin barcode-scanning app.

I also explored AI-assisted development in a GNS3 fork, using incremental specifications, code reviews and corrections. I worked on zoom, images, device grouping, text and geometric shapes. I am also working on a Rust RFC proposal for partial impl blocks.

On Redlint, now inactive, I published over 150 shorts explaining IT concepts directly. I continue learning through courses, documentation and projects, with an interest in testing, documentation, security and open-source contribution.
